thread:
sanjay: Heads-up — onboarding orca-mini-13b. I pushed weights to s3://redwood-models/orca-mini-13b/v1/ but the tokenizer appears to insert duplicate <|eos|> in some prompts. Can folks confirm weight path & the serving config I should use?

sanjay: Current local test config I'm iterating on:
```yaml
model: orca-mini-13b
weights_path: s3://redwood-models/orca-mini-13b/v1/
serving:
  continuous_batching:
    enabled: true
    max_batch_time_ms: 12
    max_batch_tokens: 1024
  cache:
    policy: prefix-kv
    ttl_seconds: 30
  generation:
    max_output_tokens: 1024
    stop_tokens: ["","<|eos|>"]
```

maria: path looks right. :eyes: the duplicate <|eos|> smells like tokenizer version mismatch — which tokenizer build are you loading? vtokenizer 0.4.1 vs 0.4.3 changed add_special_tokens behavior.

alex: FYI we've seen this before — if you call `tokenizer.encode_plus(..., add_special_tokens=True)` on top of a tokenizer that already injects EOS you'll get duplication. Quick workaround: set `add_special_tokens=False` for encode path and let serving layer append EOS once.

jen: also check `tokenizer.eos_token` vs `tokenizer.sep_token`. Some converted vocabaries set both to the same token; downstream code expects only eos.

sanjay: thanks. I'm loading tokenizer with the repo commit: `git rev-parse HEAD` -> `fa3c2d1`. When I run this locally I get this snippet in logs:
```
[INFO] prompt_tokens: 34
[INFO] appended_tokens: [",", ""]
[WARN] duplicate eos inserted by tokenizer and generator
```

phil: for serving config — given our 99th latency target of 300ms under p95 load, i'd drop `max_batch_time_ms` to 8 and `max_batch_tokens` to 768 for canary. Keeps batching but reduces tail.

maria: agree on the scheduler tweak. Also switch cache.policy to `prefix-kv` (not full-prefix) for this model; its attention patterns are prefix-heavy and we want smaller KV payloads. TTL 30s is fine.

alex: small patch suggestion: in the model adapter layer, normalize incoming prompts with:
```python
# strip explicit eos tokens at end of prompt
if prompt.endswith(tokenizer.eos_token):
    prompt = prompt[: -len(tokenizer.eos_token)]
```
Then let generator append exactly one EOS.

jen: +1 to adding a unit test that asserts no double-eos for these 3 canonical prompts. I can open the test if somebody files the issue.

sanjay: opened issue #4672 "orca-mini: tokenizer double-eos regression" and added failing example. linking here: https://redwood.internal/issue/4672 :thumbsup: 

deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled for 2026-04-02 09:00 UTC on pool `dedicated-rt-2` for model orca-mini-13b v1. Payload includes config override: `max_batch_time_ms=8`, `max_batch_tokens=768`, `cache.policy=prefix-kv`.

ci-bot: noticed unit failure `tests/tokenizer/test_double_eos.py::test_three_cases` — failing on commit fa3c2d1, pushing to PR pipeline.

sanjay: ping @alex for quick review of the adapter patch, and @jen if you can add the test. I want to get the canary out after review.

alex: grabbing review now, will try to get to it in the next hour. :coffee: 

jen: will add the test and link it to #4672, ETA end of day.

phil: once canary is up, monitor token-level error spikes and cache hit rate in dashboard `serve/orca-mini-13b/canary`. If cache hit rate drops <40% revert to no-prefix cache.

maria: noted — i'll add an alert threshold for duplicate-eos regression (rate > 0.5% over 5m) and a cache-hit alert.

sanjay: thanks everyone. i'll hold off wider rollout until canary data looks good. :pray:
